tasks.short: Identify emotional or developmental problems and tell parents.

steps.what: Watch the children for emotional or developmental signs.
Decide whether those signs are problems to raise.
Bring the problems to the parents or guardians.
Write the emotional signs on the child note.
File that note for the parents to read.

tasks.design: She still watches the child, decides whether the signs are a problem, and tells the parents herself. She writes what she saw, the child and the day once, and {WORKFLOW} files those same words on the parent record in {CRM}. A blank note files nothing, and no score of the child is produced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The worry was spoken at pickup and then typed again into a diary. A form cannot see a change in a child's play.
tasks.enabler_now: A short note can be filed as she wrote it. The watching and the conversation do not need a model.
tasks.still_hard: She has to judge a quiet week against this child's usual day, and she has to say it to the parent in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She knows the child's usual play, and she chooses the words the parent hears.
tasks.altitude: She still spends the time watching and talking. She no longer retypes a note she has finished. She does not gain a right to label a child's development.

reach.task: Hear a concern about their child
reach.learn: The diary line is the worker's own note, and only after she has already said it in person
A note exists only when the worker decided the signs were worth raising

evidence.claim: A childcare worker usually notices a change while the child is in the room, decides whether it is worth raising, tells the parent at pickup, and often writes the same observation again in a diary.
The Konnect OuderApp shows parents a timeline, a daily report in a digital diary, photos and the agenda, and asks parents for photo and diary consent at first login.
Annex III point 3 covers AI that assigns people to education and that evaluates learning outcomes.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works-council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(l).

assumptions: The child note fields are child id, date, what she saw in her own words, and who she told. She writes them in s4, and that writing stays at full time. s5 only files those stored fields, which is the mechanism that removes the retype. A blank note files nothing.

Child id and the parent contact come from the enrolment register, kept by the centre administrator. That capture sits outside this task and is not counted as saved. If the child is missing from the register, she keeps the paper note and s5 does not run.
Watching, deciding and telling the parents are unchanged, so each keeps remaining time at 100. The design does not score development and does not draft the concern.

The diary stores her words, not a rank of the child and not a time-stamp used to score her speed. Health detail in the note is special-category data. Parents are asked for diary consent before a note is visible. Where the centre is in the Netherlands and has a works council, consent for a staff tool follows WOR; elsewhere, national rules.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for a new heading on the note when the centre asks for one extra field.
unknowns: Whether parents at this centre have already consented to a diary.
Whether the worker is expected to write a note on days she also spoke at pickup.
Who follows up after the parent has been told.
research_questions: How often is the same observation written twice, once on paper and once in the diary?
Is the parent conversation always at pickup, or sometimes a booked call?

incremental.description: Add a heading to the note when the centre asks for one extra field.

approvals.approved_version: The child note as she left it in s4: child, date, what she saw, and who she told. A later edit voids the filing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype of a finished note is removed. On days she sees nothing worth raising, she writes nothing and the saving is zero. Watching, deciding and telling the parents stay at full time, so even a week with several notes stays near two points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct children in eating, resting and toilet habits.

steps.what: Notice the children at eating, resting or toilet time.
Decide which personal habits to instruct now.
Instruct the children in that health habit.

tasks.design: She still notices the moment, chooses the habit, and instructs the child at the table, the mat or the toilet. No form or message takes that over. Nothing in the design shortens those steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: The instruction happens with the child, at the moment. A card written earlier does not feed, settle or toilet a child.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need to be beside the child. There is no second writing to remove.
tasks.still_hard: Each child needs a different prompt, and the moment does not wait.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the child, times the prompt, and stays with them until the habit is done.
tasks.altitude: Her week does not change. She still instructs every habit in person and gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Keep the same habit on a day the child is at home
reach.learn: Which prompt the worker used, from what the parent heard, not from a generated plan

evidence.claim: Instructing a young child in eating, resting or toilet habits is done beside the child. A written routine does not replace the prompt at the moment, and there is usually no second record of that prompt.

assumptions: Noticing the moment, choosing the habit and instructing the child are unchanged, so each keeps remaining time at 100. No mechanism shortens any of them.
No par, checklist score or generated prompt is used. A wall card, if the centre has one, is not a record this task produces and is not counted as saved.
No tool is added, so upkeep is zero. There is no staff log and no pupil record in this task.
unknowns: Whether this centre expects any written note after a habit prompt.
Whether a parent asks for a daily line about meals or rest.
research_questions: Is any of this task's time spent writing, or is it all beside the child?

incremental.description: No tool is added on this task, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shortened. A quiet week and a week of difficult meals both stay at full time, because the work is the instruction itself.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take attendance, edit paperwork, and make phone calls.

steps.what: See which children are here for attendance.
Decide which absence needs a phone call.
Make the phone calls about those absences.
Take attendance on the room register.
Keep editing the internal paperwork by hand.
Post that attendance onto the hours sheet.

tasks.design: She still looks to see who is here, decides who to call, makes the phone calls, marks the register, and edits other paperwork by hand. {WORKFLOW} posts the marked rows onto the hours {SPREADSHEET}, and only those rows. Where the register is already the only record, nothing is posted.
tasks.previous_blocker: The headcount was marked on a room sheet and typed again onto an hours sheet. The call itself cannot be copied from a list.
tasks.enabler_now: A mark she has already made can fill the hours row. The look and the call stay hers.
tasks.still_hard: She has to see who is actually in the room, and she has to talk to the parent when a child is missing.
tasks.human_edge: She knows a late arrival from a real absence, and she handles the call.
tasks.altitude: She still counts the room and makes the calls. She no longer retypes a register she has marked. She does not invoice and she does not take payment.

reach.task: Pass registered hours to the bureau for invoicing
reach.learn: A posted row is a mark she made; a child missing from the enrolment list was written by hand and not posted

evidence.claim: Attendance is usually taken by looking around the room and marking a register. Many centres then copy those marks onto a separate hours sheet. Phone calls about an absence stay a conversation.
Gastouder childcare costs go through the bureau, by bank and not cash, on the basis of registered hours. The bureau invoices and pays.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works-council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(l).

assumptions: The register fields are child id, date, present or absent, and time in. She marks them in s4, and that marking stays at full time. s6 only posts those stored fields, which is the mechanism that removes the retype onto the hours sheet. A row with no mark is not posted.

Child id and parent phone come from the enrolment list, kept by the centre administrator. That capture sits outside this task and is not counted as saved. If a child is missing from the list, she writes the name by hand and that row is not posted.

Looking, choosing whom to call, the phone call, and editing other paperwork are unchanged, so each keeps remaining time at 100. She does not invoice and does not take cash. Where the setting is gastouder, the bureau invoices from registered hours. Where the room mark is already the only record, s6 does not run.
The hours sheet is not a score of how fast she took attendance. Where the centre is in the Netherlands and has a works council, consent for a staff tool follows WOR; elsewhere, national rules.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for matching a column when the hours sheet gains a field.
unknowns: Whether this centre keeps a second hours sheet or only the room register.
Whether the setting is a centre or a gastouder home.
Who is allowed to phone a parent about an absence.
research_questions: How often is the room register retyped onto a separate hours sheet?
Are absence calls made by the worker or by the office?

incremental.description: Match a column when the hours sheet gains a field.

approvals.approved_version: The attendance register as she marked it in s4: child, date, present or absent, and time in. A later edit voids the post.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype of a marked register onto the hours sheet is removed. Where that sheet is already the same register, the saving is zero. Looking, calling and other paperwork stay at full time, so a normal week stays near three points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Watch the children this lesson plan is for.
Choose an appropriate goal for this lesson.
Write that goal on the lesson plan note.
Draft lesson plans from that goal and library.

loop.input: The plan note she wrote: goal id, age band and interest phrase. The activity library: activity name, goal id, age band and steps. No health note and no photo.
loop.output: A lesson draft that uses her goal, her age band and one library activity, with that activity's stored steps.
loop.check: The goal sentence matches the centre plan entry for the goal she named, the activity is in the library for that age band, and the interest phrase appears only if she wrote it. A new goal, age or activity blanks the draft.
loop.stop: One pass. If the check fails or the note is blank, the draft is blank and she writes the plan.
loop.why_not_simpler: A filter on goal and age band can list activities, but her interest is free text, so the draft has to tie a library activity to that phrase.

steps.what: Check the lesson plan is developmentally appropriate.
File the checked lesson plans for the week.

tasks.design: She still watches the group and chooses the goal. She writes the goal, the age band and the interest once. A draft on {DOCS} may use only an activity already in the centre library for that goal, and she checks that it fits these children before {DOCS} files it. A blank note or a failed check leaves the draft blank.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was a blank page she filled from memory. The library, where it existed, was not tied to the goal she had chosen for this group.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can start from a goal she has named and from activities the centre already stores. She still decides what is appropriate.
tasks.still_hard: She has to know this group. A library activity can be the wrong one for these children even when the goal matches.
tasks.human_edge: She judges whether the activity fits the children she watched, and she changes it or writes her own.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the goal and checks every plan. The first draft of a plan that quotes the library can be waiting for her. She does not hand the group to a model.

reach.task: Keep the centre activity library tagged to the pedagogical plan
reach.learn: An activity with no goal id and no age band is never offered, and a missing tag leaves her writing the plan

evidence.claim: A lesson plan is usually written after the worker has watched the group. Much of the time is that judgement. The page itself often restates a goal and an activity she already knows.
Teachmate drafts early-years activity ideas from an area of learning or a child's interest, and turns practitioner notes into observation drafts. Educators stay responsible for checking.

In an EEF trial evaluated by NFER, 129 science teachers using ChatGPT with a guide cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes against 130 controls, and a blind panel saw no quality difference. Those were school science teachers, not childcare workers.
Annex III point 3 covers AI that assigns people to education and that evaluates learning outcomes.

assumptions: The plan note fields are goal id, age band and interest phrase. She writes them in s3, and that writing stays at full time. The draft may use only those fields plus the activity library. A blank note leaves the draft blank, and she writes the plan in the check, which stays at full time.

The activity library fields are activity name, goal id, age band and steps. The pedagogical lead keeps them. That upkeep is other-role time, listed below, and is not counted as her saving. An activity with no goal id is not offered. The centre pedagogical plan, also kept by the lead, holds goal id and goal text. If her goal is not in that plan, the draft is blank.

Watching the group, choosing the goal and checking the plan are unchanged, so each keeps remaining time at 100. The draft is the mechanism that shortens only the first writing of a plan that quotes the library. The filing copies the plan she has checked.

The draft does not score a child and does not assign a child to a programme. It does not receive health notes. The filed plan is the activity, not a measure of how fast she planned. Where the centre is in the Netherlands and has a works council, consent for a staff tool follows WOR; elsewhere, national rules.
Her upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for an interest phrase the library does not tag yet. The lead's library upkeep is separate and is not her time.
unknowns: Whether this centre has an activity library tagged to goal and age band.
Whether she writes a plan every week or only when the group changes.
Who may file a plan the lead has not seen.
research_questions: What share of planning time is watching the group rather than writing the page?
How often would the library have no activity for the goal she chose?

already_counted.description: She reads the draft and rejects a plan that does not fit the children she watched.

incremental.description: Note an interest phrase the library does not tag yet.
The pedagogical lead adds an activity with goal id, age band and steps when the library has a gap.

approvals.approved_version: The lesson plan as she confirmed it in s5, with her goal, her age band and the activity steps. A later edit voids the filing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the first draft of a plan that quotes a stored activity is removed, and only after she has named the goal. When the library has no match she writes the page herself and the saving is zero. Watching, choosing and checking stay at full time. A school-teacher planning trial is not this saving. A week where the library matches and she still rewrites half the page stays near eight points.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still watches the children, instructs habits in the room, and tells parents a concern in person. She marks attendance herself. A lesson draft waits for her check, and only a second copy of a note she has finished is posted.
reach: The pedagogical lead keeps the activity library, and an activity with no goal and no age band is never drafted.
The centre administrator passes registered hours on, and learns that a missing enrolment row was not posted.
The parent hears a concern from her before any diary line is filed.
skills_to_grow: Write a concern in her own words before it is filed.
Mark attendance before any hours row is posted.
Leave a lesson draft blank when the library has no activity for the goal she named.
role.ambitious_version: The week with the children is the same. The page she would have started from a blank sheet can arrive as a library draft, and she still accepts or rewrites it.
